question: A 7-month-old boy presents with fever, chills, cough, runny nose, and watery eyes. His elder brother is having similar symptoms. Past medical history is unremarkable. The patient is diagnosed with an influenza virus infection. Assuming that this is the child’s first exposure to the influenza virus, which of the following immune mechanisms will most likely function to combat this infection?

options.opa: Natural killer cell-induced lysis of virus infected cells
options.opb: Presentation of viral peptides on MHC- class I of CD4+ T cells
options.opc: Binding of virus-specific immunoglobulins to free virus
options.opd: Complement-mediated lysis of virus infected cells
options.ope: Eosinophil-mediated lysis of virus infected cells

analysis: In the context of a first exposure to the influenza virus, the primary immune mechanism that would combat the infection is the binding of virus-specific immunoglobulins to free virus. This process is mediated by antibodies produced by B cells in response to the virus, leading to neutralization and clearance of the virus from the body.
